rv.q: But after an evening in this headache-inducingly loud and bright fantasy, you may well be wishing you were home, along with Dorothy.
The show is full of imagination and skewed realities but throws too much at us and it feels like we are not so much inside Dorothy’s dream but an arcade game or hallucinatory quiz show.
It all feels a bit hollow beneath the shiny exterior, like the Tin Man’s chest cavity.
Effectively, the time-honoured appeal of L Frank Baum’s story carries the day, and what must keep us sated is the theatrical spectacle.
But her streetwise Dorothy is no ingenue, and I did miss the vulnerability that is one of the character’s obstacles to overcome.
Yet Foster’s production of this most enchanting of stories is efficient rather than inspired.
Dorothy's emotional journey from Kansas over the rainbow with all its heart-stopping courage seems to have gone AWOL in this glaring, tasteless production.
With its revisionist take Wicked defying gravity and still pulling in audiences after many years just over Green Park, it looks like audiences will be flocking to Oz in droves this summer.
Those gripes aside, few will feel shortchanged (there’s a range of reasonable pricing options) by a show that offers great songs, real spectacle and a sprinkling of starry talent.
It is very family friendly and audience reaction marks it a crowd pleaser.
Between a committed cast and those enduringly glorious songs, this is still wonderful family fun.
This fresh take on a classic remains faithful to the story we all know and love but gives it so much more.
Technically impressive with some amazing design elements and a truly wonderful cast, there is much to love about this production.
It’s a beautiful retelling which is truly hard to criticise.
The warmth of her smile, and soaring vocals in Somewhere over the Rainbow will pierce your heart.
The truly confusing mix of on-screen graphics and elaborate sets creates a dichotomy that almost undermines the enchanting quality that one might expect from Oz.

The result has not been disappointing, though. Clearly not what one would presumably expect to see in a show homaging a 1930s movie, the production has managed to keep the spark of wonder (no pun intended) that has captivated the imagination of so many children (and beyond) for almost a century now.
Clearly, a ton of creatives, effort, and money have been poured into this show, but unfortunately the production falls flat.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this high-octane revival, praising Georgina Onuorah's Dorothy and spectacular visuals while criticizing the relentless pace and overwhelming production design that some find exhausting and migraine-inducing.
